one_liner: Header-only xoshiro256++/128++ wrapper that drop-in replaces std::mt19937(_64) for <random> distributions.
what_it_does: Wraps the canonical xoshiro256++ (64-bit) and xoshiro128++ (32-bit) generators from prng.di.unimi.it as C++11-compatible engine classes usable anywhere a <random> engine such as std::mt19937_64 is expected, e.g. with std::shuffle or std::normal_distribution. It exposes the same member surface as the mersenne-twister engines: operator(), seed() (raw seed, 4-word state array, or a SeedSequence), discard(), min()/max(), and stream insertion/extraction for serialization, so most existing code needs only a type swap.
how_it_is_fast: Uses the xoshiro256++/128++ algorithm (Blackman & Vigna, 2019): a 256-bit (or 128-bit) state advanced with a few XORs, shifts and rotates per step, with a rotate-add-rotate output scrambler, no division and no large lookup tables, and a state small enough to sit in registers/L1 versus MT19937's ~2.5KB table and its tempering step. On the linked benchmark this measured 946.7M gen/s vs std::mt19937_64's 294.3M gen/s on the same hardware/compiler.
when_to_use: Need higher raw 64-bit generation throughput than std::mt19937_64 for simulations, statistical/ML model initialization, or Monte Carlo work while keeping <random>-engine compatibility (distributions, std::shuffle)
Want a much smaller generator state (32 bytes vs ~2.5KB for MT19937), e.g. per-thread or per-object RNG instances, or many concurrent generator states

Need independent parallel streams: jump()/long_jump() advance the state by the canonical 2^128/2^192-draw offsets to split into non-overlapping subsequences (both methods and the correct jump-polynomial tables are present in xoshiro.h, confirmed by reading the source this session)
Willing to vendor a single ~400-line public-domain header with no build step and no dependencies beyond the STL
Non-cryptographic use where BigCrush-class statistical quality is enough
when_not_to_use: Need cryptographic-strength randomness: xoshiro256++ is explicitly not a CSPRNG

Need output bit-for-bit reproducible with the reference prng.di.unimi.it implementation for a given integer seed: this wrapper's seed(uint64_t) path deliberately differs from the canonical seeding recipe (stated in the README)

Rely on generator equality comparisons: operator== in both classes is implemented as a bare `return std::memcmp(...)` without comparing to 0, so it reports mismatched states as equal and identical states as unequal (verified by reading xoshiro.h this session) — do not use it
Need an actively maintained or widely-adopted dependency: single-star, single-file personal project, no commits since 2021-09-08, no LICENSE file (CC0 notice only in source/README)
Need runtime-selectable, arbitrary-count independent streams the way PCG offers (per-instance odd increment); xoshiro here only offers the two fixed jump offsets

integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (per README); code compiles conditionally for C++20 to drop the explicit operator!=
integration.platforms: any — portable C++ using bit rotations and memcpy, no SIMD or architecture-specific intrinsics; benchmark itself ran on x86-64
integration.thread_safety: not documented; all state is per-instance member data with no static/global mutable state observed in xoshiro.h, so separate instances per thread should be independent, but the author makes no explicit thread-safety claim
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: true — same operator(), seed(), discard(), min()/max(), and stream insertion/extraction methods as std::mt19937_64, usable directly with <random> distributions and std::shuffle

gotchas: operator== is `return std::memcmp(...)` without `== 0`, so it evaluates backwards (identical states compare unequal, differing states compare equal) — confirmed in xoshiro.h this session; don't use it for equality checks
Default-constructed instances start from a fixed hardcoded state (not randomly seeded), the same gotcha as std::mt19937's default constructor — call seed() explicitly for non-deterministic output

Seeding logic is intentionally different from the canonical prng.di.unimi.it recipe (README: 'small change in the seeding logic'), so output won't match the reference C implementation for the same integer seed
No LICENSE file in the repo, only a CC0 dedication noted in the README and the source header comment — a compliance process that requires an actual LICENSE file will flag this
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick this over PCG (pcg-cpp / wjakob pcg32) when you specifically want the xoshiro256++ statistical profile with built-in jump()/long_jump() streams in one dependency-free header; on the same benchmark PCG's pcg64_fast is slower (763.5M/s) while pcg32_fast is faster but 32-bit only (1072M/s). If raw throughput matters more than the specific algorithm, AESRand (27-34 GB/s, requires AES-NI) or biski64 (~2.5x std::mt19937_64) beat xoshiro256++ by a wide margin on their own benchmarks.
verified_claims_summary: On zeFresk/cpp-random-benchmarks (Google Benchmark, 100 repetitions, clang -O3 -DNDEBUG, no architecture-specific flags, Intel i5-3570 @ 3.40GHz), xoshiro256++ generated 946.70M 64-bit values/s vs std::mt19937_64's 294.26M/s, about 3.2x, with both the benchmark source (src/xoshiro.cpp comparing directly against src/std.cpp) and the results table publicly readable.
status_note: Abandoned since its last commit on 2021-09-08 (1 star, 1 fork, 0 open issues, no PRs) but it's a single ~400-line CC0/public-domain header with no LICENSE file — trivial to vendor and audit, so the lack of maintenance is low-risk beyond the license-file gap.
